allies.rationale_text: Feedback-loops help red-queen-effect turn constant environmental pressure into iterative learning instead of blind acceleration.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Systems thinking focuses on understanding how parts interact and how feedback loops enable refinement. This ensures that the continuous effort is directed toward effective learning.'
allies.activation_condition: When continuous competitive adaptation requires systemic feedback mechanisms to direct learning and course correction.

allies.rationale_text: First-principles-thinking helps red-queen-effect escape stale incrementalism when conventional responses no longer keep pace with a changing baseline.
allies.source_quote: First Principles strips away the assumptions associated with conventional methods, allowing the thinker to forge a truly novel, non-obvious solution.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'When RQE forces constant running, incremental changes often fail. First Principles strips away assumptions, allowing the thinker to forge a truly novel, non-obvious solution.'
allies.activation_condition: When incremental competitive responses are insufficient and a breakthrough requires stripping assumptions to find a fundamentally novel solution.

antagonists.rationale_text: Confirmation-bias blocks red-queen-effect by making teams defend the old model instead of adapting to disconfirming competitive evidence.
antagonists.source_quote: Confirmation bias is the instinct to process information to get a conclusion we want rather than what is true, leading to model-defending behavior.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'Confirmation bias is the instinct to process information to get a conclusion we *want*... leading to model-defending behavior' — blocks necessary adaptation.
antagonists.activation_condition: When the drive to confirm existing strategies prevents recognizing that competitive dynamics demand radical adaptation.

antagonists.rationale_text: Margin-of-safety resists red-queen-effect when speed pressure would otherwise push adaptation below acceptable downside buffers.
antagonists.source_quote: Red Queen Effect conflicts with Margin Of Safety when speed pressure and continuous competitive response reduce downside buffers below acceptable thresholds.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Canonical tension: 'speed pressure and continuous competitive response reduce downside buffers below acceptable thresholds.'
antagonists.activation_condition: When competitive urgency to keep pace consumes the safety reserves needed to absorb disruption or failure.
